comment: 50yo male, chronic HCV + HBV coinfection — HCV-RNA detectable ≥6 months AND HBsAg positive ≥6 months. No current HCC, fulminant hepatitis, or HCV/HBV-associated lymphoma. Coinfection carries higher HCC incidence and a real risk of HBV reactivation / fulminant hepatitis if HCV is cured by DAA monotherapy (HCV historically suppressed HBV replication; DAA cure lifts that suppression). HCV + HBV both IARC Group 1; synergistic for HCC. Engine fires RF-CHRONIC-HCV-HBV-COINFECTION-PREVENTION (all_of: hcv_rna:detectable AND hbsag:positive) — severity critical, priority 110, takes precedence over mono-infection RFs — and routes to PreventionPlan: standard = combination antiviral (DAA e.g. sofosbuvir/velpatasvir for HCV cure + concurrent nucleos(t)ide analog entecavir or tenofovir TDF/TAF for HBV suppression) + intensified HCC surveillance (US + AFP q4-6mo per AASLD-modified protocol); alternative = HCC surveillance alone + sequential antiviral plan. Validates v0.3 §20 intensified-coinfection pathway. Anchored DIS-HCC.
